reviews.review_msg: Ash is great, I'm really grateful to have him here at SFU. If you put effort in his class, you will get a good grade. Exams are marked strictly.
How does Ash have a 4.1 on this site??? He is a terrible prof and doesn't prepare you at all for exams.

Lectures are generally pretty useless and the notes are just a mess. The notes only got better once he used another profs notes. Exams are significantly more difficult than any practice or homework he assigns. Prepare to learn everything yourself through the textbook or videos. Watch Razavi Electronics to actually get the concepts.
Rating him because he doesnt deserve such a high score on this site. Lecture pointless and did not prepare you for the tests
Class attendance was so low for this course I wonder why....

Ash is a great person and is a well-tenured professor. He has a unique teaching style and is clear about his expectations. Exam questions are often solves by no more than 4-5 lines of writing. He does tend to stick to the textbook material so attendance is not mandatory. A generous grading scale is also in place.

In his lecture I dont what he is talking about, ash dont care student, 4.4 haha big joke. I heard he was nice before that because he give the answer before exam.  you have to learn the theory by your self and I dont know why he  focus on lab thats make me laugh, no theory and lab is painful every thing google.
The best prof in ENSC.
He is best prof. at SFU. Need to do hard work for good grade. LAST course with him :(

Ash is based god. Best prof in ENSC! Clear, entertaining, always willing to help, stays late to help students in the lab (labs are tough but rewarding). If you put in the work he makes it easy to get a good grade. Wants everyone to succeed. Great guy. Sense of humour is second to none. classic. non "el cheapo" education with this guy!
Ash is the best! So sad this will probably be my last class with him :(

Ash is easily the most engaging engineering professor I've had so far. Yes, his notes may be a bit messy, but he points out important points that students should know for exams, labs and homework. He's helpful in labs and gives adequate feedback.

I am not sure why his rating is this high, but he never hold office hour and the TA he hired was beyond horrible. He cares about the student a lot and is a nice guy. His notes are horrible, scattered over the places. Passionate about his teaching and scales well. Hard exam.
Best prof ever. Always willing to help students. I wish all the ENSC profs were like him
AWESOME PROFF. If every prof at SFU was more like Ash than it'd be the best school in Canada.

Amazing prof! He's very enthusiastic, his lectures were incredibly clear, quizzes were fair, but a bit tricky, and he is always willing to help and explain concepts we may find difficult. Sometimes came in on weekends to help with our labs and answer questions before exams. Take any course you can with him. Curves high, don't piss him off.
Great Prof. Motivates you to be an engineer. Spends alot of time with students. Scales the grades very well at the end.
What happens in Vegas, stays in Vegas...

Was gonna come here and say what everyone else has to say so ill try and make mine different. If he every stopped teaching, it would be a great loss to SFU. Not only did i learn so much, i will never forget him. He honesstly made me believe that my education was the object of his life. And he has that effect on every student.
Amazing professor. Tests are very fair. He always has these weird stories to tell us, really funny.
The best professor ever! No words! Take the courses with Ash...
Best prof ever, completly changed my view towards electronics and engineering, very caring and helpful. very fair and funny! love him
Intelligent, enthusiastic, patient, and caring. Exams are a bit tricky and hard to study for. Nonetheless, he is great at teaching.
I love him to death.

Literally the best prof I've ever had. Unlike so many other profs, Ash shows enthusiasm and care for his students. His exams may be hard but the things you'll learn from him is well worth it. Take his classes if you have the chance to, you'd be happy that you did.

So great! You really have a chance to "learn" staff from his lectures. friendly and nice. exame is fun and challenge, average is not too high, but he does scale alot. (B- to A+). if u ever have a chace. don't miss!
SFU wont be the same without him, 1 of the best prof ive ever met, If you have the chance, take his classes, you wont regret
never understood what he says and what he teaches and never will
very nice and helpfull. Please oh please don't make us write out full lab writeups. Why can't results and discussion be enough?????
No Comments
Ash is the Man
very nice guy..
No Comments
funny lecture, nice...............

Not a bad teacher... tries to stay happy all the time in class and likes to know everyone by their names. Extremely helpful in her office hrs and has very fair exams. Labs are incredibly time consuming though, but interesting. Bottom line: No one can replace Ash but she still did a great job! I recommend her.

She simply copies the textbook to the overhead...no clear explanation. I skiped almost all classes after the first two weeks...there's really no point of going to lecture...But she's nice to students, which is the only good thing of her...Exams are fair.
Slides are unhelpful and not clear; lack annotation and context. Due to this, it is often times unhelpful to sit through his lectures.

He's actually a solid prof, all the exam questions are from the practice behind textbook, and there is a youtube channel solving these questions. Overall his pace a lit bit slower than other prof lab is basically free mark you just follow the material. Exam grades come out fast 9/10

Majid is a good professor in terms of teaching. However, he gives way too much work. In his labs, he requires you to complete the lab itself, write a lab report, and perform a lab demo. In addition, you still need to do his hw assignments and study for his midterms. You won't have any free time considering how much work he gives you.
Some of the tutorials have been of limited use because Majid has provided the TAs with incorrect material on very short notice.
Some of the tutorials have been of limited use because Majid has provided the TAs with incorrect material on very short notice.

After 252 last year, I was dreading taking another class with him. However, Majid has greatly improved as a professor. Quizzes, tests, and labs were all fair and generously marked. The only issue were the unscheduled mandatory lab sessions on Friday mornings for which I had to skip another class.

Majid went from being hated in ENSC252 in Fall 22' to becoming one of the greatest profs I've had. His explanations of concepts were always clear and it just clicks. However, you will still need to put in time practicing questions to do well in this class. Only downside is the lab sessions are chaotic and labs have unclear/wrong steps.

Majid is a nice guy. He has some bad habits like picking on students in class, not posting notes, or explaining concepts in ways difficult to understand. However, he is not bad at teaching and wants his students to succeed. I enjoyed the labs and tutorials by TAs were helpful. The quiz and exam averages were low 40s, but he scales nicely (to a B).

He is one of the best professors I ever had in Microelectronics. He has a great passion for teaching and excellent at teaching the material and is very good at getting concepts across. The lectures were great. The exams were very fair.
Majid is a great prof! He is very willing to help during and outside of class. The course itself was hard enough, but he made it easy to understand by bringing real-life examples during the lectures.

Taken a class with him in the past and he has significantly improved. I have gained more respect for him over time as I found that he's very approachable and open to answering any questions or concerns you may have. Do not expect to understand everything on the first go of lectures. It's university and the concepts are hard. Allocate time to study.

Difficulty was definitely 5/5 but, unless you put in absolutely no work he wouldn't fail you because he scales hard as he doesn't want students to fail. He is a caring prof and would recommend going up to him after class and ask questions if needed.
Majid is a very knowledgable prof in engineering Science. Very good lectures.

Majid is s by far one of the most caring professors I have had. He is very helpful outside of the class even not on his office hours he is always ready to be helpful. He is very knowledgeable and relates the course materials with practical examples.

Not the worst prof. He is a bit dry, but if you pay attention he's pretty helpful. Open to questions outside of class as well, and wants you to succeed. Don't be afraid to ask him questions - he's not as intimidating as he seems. To do well just redo assignment and tutorial questions.
Terrible Professor. Refuses to post lecture notes and can't explain topics to save his life

Very knowledgeable, Bring practical example into the class. I would recommend taking the course. He's very thorough in the notes. I would recommend attending lectures and starting the homework early. The homework is almost entirely based on notes or textbook.

Majid is an easy professor to talk to and is always approachable. Whenever in person, always makes time to get clarification on a topic, and would go through very detailed descriptions on not only the solution, but correlations towards real engineering discussions.

I personally didn't enjoy his lectures. However, if you enjoy professors that don't clearly explain what they're teaching and is vague than you might like his lectures more than I did. His labs are strenuously long and aren't worth much of your grade and often have incorrect instructions. In general, his class structure is very poor but he's nice.

Not a terrible prof, not the best either. Does go over derivations that textbook skips, and exams are pretty fair overall. However, is slightly disorganized and lectures were often a bit behind labs. Is very open to student suggestions, I requested extra office hours before an exam and he arranged for TAs to hold one. Responds well to emails.

Lectures are copy-pasted from textbook. Assignments are long and often given before material is covered. Labs are long, hard, directions are unclear and don't benefit your learning. Exams are hard and a ridiculous amount of your grade, formulas are often not given. Avoid taking him at all costs, and wait for another prof even if delays your degree.

Great and caring professor. Grades are based on 3 exams, assignments, quizzes, and lab experiments. ENSC225 is a new and tough subject for me, but he is one of the best to teach it so I certainly recommend him.

The professor gives us s fundamental understanding of pn junction, BJT, and MOSFET. It is beneficial to me for further study. Exams' difficulties are the same as the examples he is solving during the lecture times and assignments' questions. I highly appreciate this professor and his courses.

Honestly he's not a horrible lecturer but dear god. The labs are worth nothing compared to how much work they take. On top of that they are filled with unclear guidelines and I've gotten more help from other profs during the lab than Majid. He is still new but if he works this stuff out he would probably make a decent prof.

Terrible at explaining the core concepts of the course material, and regularly dodges questions about course material and concepts. Majid's labs are riddled with errors and refuses to fix these errors, instead expecting students to realize that the lab instructions as given will not lead to the desired result and ignore/alter the instructions.
Majid is a knowledgeable, caring and approachable lecturer. He is a great lecturer, and always has practical industry-related examples for the course materials (ENSC225).
Awesome prof, don't care about those comments bellow.

His lectures are taken directly from the textbook. It's honestly better to simply read the book than attempt to follow his lecture notes. The error riddled labs with their vague instructions also take an unacceptable amount of time considering how little they are worth for the class. These labs however are still mandatory to do, or else you fail.
poorly organized, bad memory about sfu
Do yourself a favor. Avoid him for this course please! thank you.
hard class. boring lectures. I did not like his teaching style and exam pattern at all.
Too lazy to write his own notes.only 4 questions on final only from high freq mosfets and BJT. So I suppose he thinks amplifier diodes etc were meant just to pass our time
Half of the class dropped the course in the first week of classes.The 75% of the rest remaining failed the class. not recommended at all.
Final was a killer and an extremely low average of 32%. Well why do you think that happened? Think.
it was a bad experience  to do this course with Dr.Syrzycki because he would not scale. bad. like sooo bad. like O M G bad!!!!!
Dr.Marek may be a very knowledgeable person but he wasn't able to transfer that knowledge to us and gave a really hard final exam. overall course load was not so much.
will turn out to be a nightmare. refrain from taking such an important course with Dr.Marek.
Correct! it was the most ridiculous grading I have seen so far.
TA's were more helpful in this course. Marek had zero contribution and 100% expectation.
32% average on the final exam yet he does not want to scale.
re-taking it with ash. Im sorry to say but he is bad professor! Funny guy though.
Poor teaching skills and grading is even worse
he is one of those who cannot digest that he's a bad teacher and students have to pay fr that because he would not scale. WORST PROF IN Engineering so far.

He points flaws in the textbook recommended by him. Average of class was less than 40%, but he didn't scale. Encourages you to ask questions, but once you ask a question, he doesn't understand it and then basically tries his level best to make you look stupid. Pointless true/false quizzes. Unimaginably difficult final. AVOID. At all costs.
Very hard class. He assumes that we know everything. i think learning from the book is easier than understanding him.
He may have a hard to understand accent but he is a smart and good professor. Makes class interesting to the best of his ability!
very sad and extremely disappointed with his teaching
Can't understand anything he's trying to say.
Whiny high-pitched voice means you can hardly understand him. Notes not good, teaching style much like ash except slower
easy midterm, but didn't learn much from him.
Almost impossible to understand. Writing dreadfully small. But test u by the textbook.
One of the best profs I've ever had. Explains the concepts very well. He's very organized. Exams are fair, but there are always a couple of unexpected questions. Homework and labs are easy.
His midterm is easy, but the final is a little challenging. As long as you know the basic concepts you'll be doing fine on exams.

Very good instructor.  Does a good job of conveying the important concepts and goes through the details of solving complicated problems well.  The lab requirements for the course were a bit hefty, but overall not a bad course.
He's so nice
solid guy; puts notes online and doesn't speak much.
When I'm trying to find a place to sleep, I can always count on Michael Adachi's voice to knock me right out, solid 10/10
Terrible.
Michael Adachi is by far the greatest professor I've ever had at SFU, a god send to humanity.
Just copies notes the whole time, great prof , would definitely take again
This has been by far the most useless course I have ever taken. Man means well, but you're basically reading the entire book in lecture
I loved the easy way he conducted the complex materials.
Awesome
